content:
maria: Heads-up — ranky3b-v2 onboarding results are weird: offline eval NDCG +1.8 but MRR -3.5 against baseline. Shadow in prod shows similar MRR drop. Anyone have ideas?

kevin: Saw the same in the nightly report. Quick numbers: eval on holdout (100k queries): ndcg@10 +1.8, mrr@10 -3.5. Shadow (10k) mrr -3.1.

jason: Two quick suspects: candidate ordering differences between eval and prod, and quantization tie-breaking. Eval harness sorts candidates by retrieval score before rerank; prod preserves original retrieval ordering. Ties can flip top-1 which kills MRR.

maria: Good call. I pushed a branch to run eval preserving retrieval order (no pre-sort). Kicking off a run now.

ops-bot: shadow-job 1736000001 finished: 10k queries. Result summary attached: ndcg@10 +1.6, mrr@10 -0.5 when preserving retrieval order.

eva: So ordering explains most of the MRR regression (3.0 points). Remaining ~0.5 could be quantization noise. What quant config did we run?

kevin: PTQ int8 config we used (from model-onboard/quant-config.yaml):
```
bits: 8
method: per-channel
calibration-batches: 256
calibration-metric: l2
symmetric: true
```

maria: Re-ran float32 (no quant) but preserving retrieval order: ndcg@10 +1.7, mrr@10 +0.2. So float32 gives +0.2 MRR; int8 gives -0.5; delta ~0.7 MRR from quantization.

jason: That suggests quant ties or tiny logit perturbations are changing top prediction ordering. Quick hack: add tiny gaussian jitter to logits before softmax in eval to see sensitivity.

maria: Ran with jitter sigma=1e-6. Newnumbers: ndcg@10 +1.6, mrr@10 +0.1. Jitter restores most of the MRR.

kevin: OK that's a clear signal: quantized model has many near-ties at top ranks. Tiebreaker behavior differs between float and int ops. Two pragmatic fixes: (A) change reranker to use stable comparison on (score, retrieval_rank) to prefer earlier candidates when scores equal within epsilon; (B) apply small random epsilon at export/inference for quant runs.

maria: Proposed action items: 1) Add preserve_retrieval_order flag in eval harness (default false to not break existing workflows). 2) Add tiny deterministic epsilon step for quant models (seeded RNG) or explicit tie comparator. 3) Add unit test with synthetic tie cases so this won't regress. I'll open PR with tests and benchmark rerun artifacts. cc @jason @eva

jason: Please include a small reproducible example. Example (JSON) of input that reproduced flip: 
```
{
  "query": "how to reset password",
  "candidates": [
    {"id": "c1", "retrieval_rank": 1, "retrieval_score": 12.34, "text": "..."},
    {"id": "c2", "retrieval_rank": 2, "retrieval_score": 12.10, "text": "..."}
  ]
}
```
And a comparator change: `if abs(score_a - score_b) < 1e-6 then return retrieval_rank_a < retrieval_rank_b`

maria: I'll include that comparator and the jitter option behind a config flag. Also updating the model card to document quant sensitivity and the eval note.

eva: :thumbsup: can we also add a small note in the onboard checklist: "run both sorted-by-score and original-order evals" so teams don't miss ordering issues in the future.

maria: yup adding checklist item. Will post PR link here when ready.

kevin: Thanks — nice root cause. Once PR lands, let's rerun the full 100k holdout to confirm final numbers and update the release notes.

maria: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-onboard/pull/1234 — includes tests, docs, and benchmark rerun artifacts.
